requirement.evidence: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
requirement.note: Also supported: landlord use ban in 98.1103(b) and tenant remedies in 98.1104 (injunctive relief, damages, civil penalties up to $1,000, attorney's fees). The card says "set or recommend"; the definition covers devices that advise or recommend rates.

key_value.note: The $1,000 cap appears in 98.1104(a): "civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation". The card's per-month and per-property language applies to landlord use under 98.1103(b).

effective_date.note: Field is empty on the card.

status.note: The document is a proposed ordinance with a blank final passage date and a blank adoption certification. It presents the ordinance as proposed, not adopted, so "pending" fits. The document does not say whether it was later adopted as of 2026-10-01.

coverage.note: Field is empty on the card. The document lists no unit thresholds or construction cutoffs.

citation.evidence: Amend San Diego Municipal Code Chapter 9, Article 8 by adding new Division 11, sections 98.1101, 98.1102, 98.1103, and 98.1104, to adopt the proposed Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance.
citation.note: Section 98.1103 and ordinance number O-2025-107 match the document. The remedies are in 98.1104, which the card's range covers.
